summary: Clip-on toilet sensor and subscription app for digestive and urinary wellness tracking.
editor_note: Passive measurement is an alternative to keeping a bathroom diary. Throne describes a clip-on sensor that recognizes a paired phone, captures a session, and sends analysis to a paid app. Practical questions precede the charts: toilet fit, user identification, and cloud processing of sensitive observations. This is a general-wellness product, not a diagnostic test. Independent validation matters more than the number of AI models behind it.

sources.label: Throne Science how it works page

product_evidence.claim: Throne describes motion-triggered activation followed by Bluetooth recognition of a paired phone, camera and acoustic capture of the session, and cloud processing before results appear in the app.
The setup guide specifies Wi-Fi connectivity and compatibility with white toilets whose rims are up to 2.25 inches thick; it also documents manual session-start buttons when a phone is absent.

The science page describes stool-form classification, optical urine-color estimates, session timing, and acoustic urinary-flow analysis; it labels the product for general wellness, not disease diagnosis or treatment.
Throne's support page says a paid membership is required for full functionality, including app analysis and cloud history; canceling membership stops analysis and app syncing.

market_context.primary_user: Consumers who want an at-home record of digestive and urinary patterns and are willing to use compatible hardware, a phone, Wi-Fi, and an ongoing membership.
market_context.differentiation: A toilet-mounted sensor automates routine session capture and combines it with longitudinal app analysis, rather than relying entirely on self-entered diaries or mailed samples.
market_context.why_now: The July 2026 Series A and public setup and membership documentation make practical household use and retention observable questions, separate from future clinical applications.

risks.claim: Vendor accuracy claims, physician endorsements, and general research about bathroom habits do not by themselves establish independent validation of this device or improved health outcomes.
risks.basis: The science page pairs performance claims with a general-wellness disclaimer. This review did not reproduce tests or assess a complete independent device-validation study.

risks.claim: Household identification reliability, fit, and sensitive-data handling require testing beyond public documentation; clinician endorsements are not evidence of routine clinical deployment.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment of the paired-phone workflow, compatibility requirements, cloud processing, and physician material. No hardware was installed or tested.

risks.claim: The homepage and support article show slightly different hardware and monthly prices, so this profile states the membership requirement without asserting a single current checkout total.
risks.basis: Both official pages were reviewed; an actual checkout, regional taxes, shipping, and final subscription terms were not verified.
